high.title: Vietnam Set to Have First Bank with Capital Over 110,000 Billion VND, But Not a "Big 4"
high.summary: Techcombank (TCB) has approved a massive capital increase plan that would make it Vietnam's largest bank by charter capital. The bank plans to issue nearly 4.29 billion shares, including 4.25 billion shares (60% of current outstanding shares) from retained earnings and 35.9 million ESOP shares. This would increase Techcombank's charter capital from 70.862 trillion VND to 113.739 trillion VND, surpassing traditional "Big 4" banks. For VND traders and bond investors, this represents a significant shift in Vietnam's banking landscape, potentially affecting interbank rates and credit allocation. The capital expansion could strengthen Techcombank's lending capacity and market position, while the large share issuance may impact stock liquidity and foreign ownership ratios in the banking sector.

high.title: State Bank of Vietnam Wants to Amend Regulations Related to Trillions of VND in Banking System, Experts Worry About Impact on Profitability and Credit Growth
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam has proposed significant changes to Circular 22/2019, which governs safety ratios in banking operations. Key changes include replacing the Loan-to-Deposit Ratio (LDR) with Credit-to-Deposit Ratio (CDR) and introducing Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR) requirements aligned with Basel III standards. The new CDR will only count retail deposits (market 1) as eligible funding sources while excluding loans funded by equity capital. This regulatory shift could significantly constrain credit growth and impact bank profitability, as it tightens the calculation of available funding for lending. For FX and bond markets, this could mean reduced liquidity in the banking system and potential upward pressure on lending rates as banks adjust to stricter funding requirements.

high.title: Former Deputy Governor Dao Minh Tu Appointed Vice Chairman and Secretary General of Vietnam Banking Association Term VIII
high.summary: Former Standing Deputy Governor Dao Minh Tu has been elected Vice Chairman and Secretary General of the Vietnam Banking Association for Term VIII (2026-2031). This appointment represents continuity in banking sector leadership, as Tu previously served as Standing Deputy Governor from 2012-2022 and was instrumental in key monetary policy decisions. His new role could influence banking industry coordination and policy implementation, particularly regarding regulatory compliance and international integration. For FX markets, his experience with exchange rate management and capital flow supervision could provide stability in policy coordination between SBV and commercial banks.

medium.title: US Inflation Ghost Looms: Government Issues Bonds with Highest Yield in 19 Years, Markets Shaken by 80% Fed Rate Hike Probability
medium.summary: US Treasury issued $25 billion of 30-year bonds at 5.046% yield, the highest since 2005, after April wholesale inflation surged to 6%. Producer Price Index showed strongest gains since 2022, driven by Middle East conflict pushing energy costs higher. Market pricing indicates 80% probability of Fed rate hikes. This could impact Vietnam through capital flow reversals if US yields continue rising.

medium.title: Vietcombank, VietinBank, Agribank, BIDV Halt All Withdrawal/Transfer Transactions for 5 Following Cases
medium.summary: Major Vietnamese banks are implementing new SBV regulations requiring biometric data and updated identification documents. Customers who haven't completed these updates face transaction suspensions including cash withdrawals, transfers, and online payments. This reflects SBV's enhanced KYC/AML compliance measures that could temporarily reduce banking system liquidity.

medium.title: One Stock Faces Delisting Risk: Over 500 Billion VND Accumulated Losses, Multiple Consecutive Quarters with No Revenue
medium.summary: HNX announced DDG stock faces mandatory delisting due to three consecutive years of losses (2023-2025) and qualified audit opinions. Company recorded 336 billion VND loss in 2025 with revenue dropping from 358 billion to 70 billion VND, showing severe business deterioration.

medium.title: State Bank of Vietnam Conducts Asset and Income Verification Lottery at Agencies and Units for 2026
medium.summary: SBV conducted public lottery to select agencies for asset and income verification as part of anti-corruption measures. This demonstrates continued focus on transparency and governance within the central banking system, reinforcing institutional credibility.
